title: Strictification and signed dual presentation of bounded localized complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Use sheaves of $R$-modules, their derived category $D(R)$, and the scalar localization $Q_t:D(R)\to D(R)[1/t]$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal C)$ and $Q_t^0:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M[1/t]$ for raw scalar localization of this $A$-linear module-sheaf category. Every cochain complex $\overline P$ in $\mathcal M[1/t]$ that is zero outside $[a,b]$ admits a cochain complex $P$ in $\mathcal M$, zero outside the same interval and with the same underlying module objects in degrees $r\in[a,b]$ (the integral terms outside this interval are chosen to be zero), and a chain isomorphism $(Q_t^0)_*P\cong\overline P$. In particular their images in the derived category of $\mathcal M[1/t]$ are isomorphic. Localized finite-free-retract presentations of the terms are preserved by this identification; no lift of the retraction maps themselves is required. This assertion allows nonzero $t$-power-torsion defects in chosen numerators of successive localized differentials.  For an actual $P$ as above, or any cochain complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves, zero outside an integer interval $[a,b]$. Suppose that for each $r\in[a,b]$ there are $m_r\geq0$ and morphisms $i_r:Q_t(P^r[0])\to Q_t(R^{\oplus m_r}[0])$ and $p_r:Q_t(R^{\oplus m_r}[0])\to Q_t(P^r[0])$ with $p_ri_r=1$. These are degreewise localized retractions; no integral or chain-level splitting is assumed. Fix a K-injective resolution $j:R[0]\to I$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and set $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$, $T=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Then the surviving Hom projections identify
$$D^q=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-q},R),\qquad d_D^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-q-1},\qquad D^q=0\quad(q\notin[-b,-a]).$$
For every $q$, $Q_t(D^q[0])$ admits a retraction from $Q_t(R^{\oplus m_{-q}}[0])$, taking $m_r=0$ outside $[a,b]$. For each $r$, postcomposition with $j$ gives an isomorphism
$$Q_t\bigl(\mathcal Hom_R(P^r,R)[0]\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_t\bigl(\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P^r[0],I)\bigr).$$
The actual chain map $c_P:D\to T$ is postcomposition with $j$, natural contravariantly under chain maps in $P$; the single-term comparisons are natural under module maps and their $A[1/t]$-linear extensions. In particular, $D$ is a bounded complex with the allowed localized finite-free-retract terms, before any assertion that $Q_t(c_P)$ is invertible.

proof.text: First treat the lifting assertion. Abbreviate $Q_t^0$ to $Q^0$. By [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor], each localized Hom module is the fraction module of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Explicitly $u\otimes(c/t^n)\mapsto cu/t^n$; tensor balancing gives the inverse $u/t^n\mapsto u\otimes t^{-n}$. If $a>b$, all objects are zero and the zero complex gives the assertion. Otherwise write the finitely many differentials $\overline d^r$ ($a\leq r<b$) as $f_r/t^{e_r}$. Let $e=\max(\{0\}\cup\{e_r\})$ and replace $f_r$ by $t^{e-e_r}f_r$, so every $\overline d^r=t^{-e}Q^0(f_r)$. Set $f_r=0$ outside that range. This includes $a=b$, when there are no differentials.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization); Tags 07JZ and 07K0 (definition-localization-module, lemma-universal-property-localization-module). The finite denominator and defect calculation is agent-written.

proof.text: The complex relation gives $t^{-2e}Q^0(f_{r+1}f_r)=0$, hence $Q^0(f_{r+1}f_r)=0$. By the fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], for each $a\leq r\leq b-2$ there is $N_r\geq0$ with $t^{N_r}f_{r+1}f_r=0$ in the original Hom module. Choose $N=\max(\{0\}\cup\{N_r\})$ and define $P^r=\overline P^r$ for $a\leq r\leq b$ and $P^r=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ (a term $\overline P^r$ with $r\notin[a,b]$ is only a zero object of $\mathcal M[1/t]$ and may be a nonzero $t$-power-torsion sheaf in $\mathcal M$, for instance any object when $t$ is nilpotent), and $d_P^r=t^N f_r$. Then $d_P^{r+1}d_P^r=t^{2N}f_{r+1}f_r=t^{2N-N_r}(t^{N_r}f_{r+1}f_r)=0$. Outside the indicated finite range the composite contains a zero map. Thus this is an actual complex on the same objects, zero outside $[a,b]$; no numerator was assumed to square to zero before this multiplication.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization); Tags 07JZ and 07K0 (definition-localization-module, lemma-universal-property-localization-module). The finite denominator and defect calculation is agent-written.

proof.text:
Set $h=e+N$. For $a\leq r\leq b$ put $s^r=t^{h(b-r)}1_{\overline P^r}$, a morphism in $\mathcal M[1/t]$, and use the unique zero-object isomorphisms outside $[a,b]$. These components give $s:(Q^0)_*P\to\overline P$, since
$$s^{r+1}Q^0(d_P^r)=t^{h(b-r-1)+N}Q^0(f_r)=t^{h(b-r)-e}Q^0(f_r)=\overline d^r s^r.$$
Every $s^r$ is invertible, with inverse $t^{-h(b-r)}1$, so the componentwise inverse is a chain inverse. Their images remain inverse after passing to the derived category. Retractions of a term transport by $i\mapsto i(s^r)^{-1}$ and $p\mapsto s^r p$, whose composite is $1$. This transports existing localized retractions and does not lift them to integral maps.

proof.text: For the remaining assertions take any actual bounded $P$. Apply [lem-sc-hom-complex-to-single] to $L=P$, $N=R$: its surviving product projection identifies $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$ with the signed dual of [def-sc-signed-sheaf-dual-complex]. Thus $D^q=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-q},R)$ and $d_D^q(\phi)=-(-1)^q\phi d_P^{-q-1}=(-1)^{q+1}\phi d_P^{-q-1}$. If $q\notin[-b,-a]$, then $P^{-q}=0$, and a map from the zero module is zero, giving $D^q=0$. No exactness or projectivity assertion is used in this identification. For the explicitly normalized projections, use [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]: the normalized projection is homComplexπ composed with the single degree-zero identification. Its product universal property makes the sole nonzero factor invertible, and its differential equation gives the same displayed sign after transporting the single complex degree-zero term. The sole surviving product projection is invertible by the existing proved RationalTermHom.soleFactorIsIso, imported for proof access; no second proof of this product lemma is introduced.

proof.text: For each $r\in[a,b]$ apply [lem-sf-rational-term-hom-comparison] with $F=P^r$ and the displayed $i_r,p_r$. Its hypotheses are precisely retractions in $D(R)[1/t]$, so no integral splitting is needed. It gives both the invertibility of the stated postcomposition map $Q_t(\mathcal Hom_R(P^r,R)[0])\to Q_t(\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P^r[0],I))$ and a retraction of its source from $Q_t(R^{\oplus m_r}[0])$. Taking $r=-q$ gives the asserted retraction for $Q_t(D^q[0])$. Outside $[a,b]$ take $F=0$, $m_r=0$ and the unique maps between zero objects; the same lemma applies. Its final clause supplies naturality under module maps and their $A[1/t]$-linear extensions.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product projections and differential; Tags 08JI and 08JJ motivate the finite-summand comparison, whose scalar-localized version is the cited existing node.

proof.text: By the covariant chain-map functoriality in [def-pur-hom-complex], postcomposition with $j$ gives the actual chain map $c_P:D\to T$. Explicitly $(c_P^q\phi)^u=j^{u+q}\phi^u$. Since $d_Ij=jd_{R[0]}$, the defining Hom differential gives $d_T(j\phi)=j\,d_D(\phi)$. For a chain map $v:P'\to P$, precomposition and postcomposition commute: $(j\phi)v=j(\phi v)$ componentwise, which is the asserted contravariant naturality square. These formulas also show that this map uses the single-term comparisons already specified. The bounded support and localized finite-free-retract terms of $D$ were established in the preceding steps; none of these conclusions asserts invertibility of $Q_t(c_P)$ for a general bounded $P$.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Use sheaves of $R$-modules, their derived category $D(R)$, and the scalar localization $Q_t:D(R)\to D(R)[1/t]$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal C)$ and $Q_t^0:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M[1/t]$ for raw scalar localization of this $A$-linear module-sheaf category. Every cochain complex $\overline P$ in $\mathcal M[1/t]$ that is zero outside $[a,b]$ admits a cochain complex $P$ in $\mathcal M$, zero outside the same interval and with the same underlying module objects, and a chain isomorphism $(Q_t^0)_*P\cong\overline P$. In particular their images in the derived category of $\mathcal M[1/t]$ are isomorphic. Localized finite-free-retract presentations of the terms are preserved by this identification; no lift of the retraction maps themselves is required. This assertion allows nonzero $t$-power-torsion defects in chosen numerators of successive localized differentials.  For an actual $P$ as above, or any cochain complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves, zero outside an integer interval $[a,b]$. Suppose that for each $r\in[a,b]$ there are $m_r\geq0$ and morphisms $i_r:Q_t(P^r[0])\to Q_t(R^{\oplus m_r}[0])$ and $p_r:Q_t(R^{\oplus m_r}[0])\to Q_t(P^r[0])$ with $p_ri_r=1$. These are degreewise localized retractions; no integral or chain-level splitting is assumed. Fix a K-injective resolution $j:R[0]\to I$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and set $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$, $T=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Then the surviving Hom projections identify
$$D^q=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-q},R),\qquad d_D^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-q-1},\qquad D^q=0\quad(q\notin[-b,-a]).$$
For every $q$, $Q_t(D^q[0])$ admits a retraction from $Q_t(R^{\oplus m_{-q}}[0])$, taking $m_r=0$ outside $[a,b]$. For each $r$, postcomposition with $j$ gives an isomorphism
$$Q_t\bigl(\mathcal Hom_R(P^r,R)[0]\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_t\bigl(\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P^r[0],I)\bigr).$$
The actual chain map $c_P:D\to T$ is postcomposition with $j$, natural contravariantly under chain maps in $P$; the single-term comparisons are natural under module maps and their $A[1/t]$-linear extensions. In particular, $D$ is a bounded complex with the allowed localized finite-free-retract terms, before any assertion that $Q_t(c_P)$ is invertible.
statement_change.what: The same underlying module objects can only be retained inside [a,b]. Outside it an object can be zero in the raw localized category while nonzero integrally: e.g. a nonzero Z/2 module outside the interval with A=Z and t=2, or any nonzero object for t=0. Requiring both the same integral objects everywhere and integral zero support is false. This corrects only that phrase to match the already-reviewed proof[1] and proof[2], which explicitly set integral terms to zero outside the interval. Added statement dependencies expose the existing signed-dual, normalized term-comparison definitions and canonical coefficient-action interfaces used in the Lean statement.
